finalText:
Redis died at 02:14:07 (`10.0.0.12:6379` refused connections). The app fell back to hitting the store directly, and that triggered a cache miss storm.

From there the request queue never stopped growing, from 52 up to 568 requests, while every request timed out after 5 seconds. Redis reconnect attempts kept failing every ~80 seconds, all the way through attempt 12 at 02:31:26.

The pile-up finally broke things at 02:31:44: worker-2 ran out of memory and got restarted, then the api process stopped responding entirely. The supervisor killed the whole process group at 02:31:52, and that's the outage.

So it's one chain: Redis went down, nothing gave the queue a limit or a circuit breaker, and it ran the service out of memory. Getting Redis back up won't be enough on its own, since the queue had no cap to stop this from happening again.
